description:
THE BLUNT ALTERNATIVE TO contact-dribble-cancel-early.json. ONE RE-AIMED LOAD. Halves EVERY cancel gate inside a stagger at once. Apply this INSTEAD of the headline pack, never as well - see COLLISIONS.

WHAT IT IS FOR. contact-dribble-cancel-early.json fixes one specific injustice: the ball carrier is routed to the LAST cancel keyframe while everyone else uses the first. This pack does not fix that asymmetry - it just makes the whole stagger family more responsive by halving every gate in the function. Use it if you want the stagger to stop eating input across the board rather than only correcting the Dribble case, or as the A/B partner for the headline pack so you can feel which mechanism you prefer.

WHAT CHANGES. Every cancel keyframe query in match::anime::action::Stagger::vf14 (0x143f00de0) is divided by a playback-speed scale passed in xmm2. The function loads that scale as a literal 1.0f at exactly ONE instruction, 0x143f00e13, into xmm6, and then copies xmm6 into xmm2 before each of its four keyframe calls (0x143f00e25, 0x143f00e47, 0x143f00ea7, 0x143f00f2a). Re-aiming that single load to the existing read-only 2.0f cell halves every gate. THE HOUSE TECHNIQUE APPLIES AND MUST NOT BE SHORT-CUT: the 1.0f cell at 0x1478502b8 has 13,240 referrers image-wide. It is NOT written. Only this one instruction's disp32 moves. Census run this pass: 0x1478502b8 refcount=13240 writers=0; the 2.0f target 0x147850490 refcount=2014 writers=0, both read-only shared literals.

MEASURED EFFECT (a-EMULATED, this pass, through the REAL requester 0x143eb4f40 -> vf2 -> Stagger::vf14 -> starter). Frame at which a request may start out of a stagger, test motion with cancel keys at frames 16/32/48:
    scale            Move/Trap/Tackle    Dribble
    1.0f  STOCK            16              48
    1.5f                   11              32
    2.0f  THIS PACK         8              24
    3.0f                    5              16
The frame numbers are proportional and exact - the gate is linear in this scale.

WHICH VALUE. 2.0f is chosen deliberately over a 'safe' 1.25f or 1.5f: a 25% change to a lock you cannot measure in seconds is not something anyone can judge in two halves, and this project's packs have repeatedly shipped first values too weak to notice. 2.0f halves the whole window and is unmistakable. If it feels floaty, the gentler 1.5f cell is 0x147850340 (806 referrers, writers 0) - patch bytes F30F1035258F9403 - and the stronger 3.0f cell is 0x1478504e8.

HOW IT KEEPS THE WEIGHT - AND WHERE IT IS WEAKER THAN THE HEADLINE PACK. The stagger animation is NOT shortened: this touches only the frame at which input stops being discarded, not the clip, not its selection, not its severity. But be clear about the difference in kind. The headline pack moves Dribble onto a keyframe the animators actually authored as a cancel point. This pack moves every request to a keyframe that is half of an authored one - a number nobody designed. That is why it is the alternative and not the recommendation.

EVIDENCE.
  a-EMULATED - the scale sweep above, on the game's own bytes under Unicorn. Harness tools/emu_contact_request.py (section 8) and tools/emu_contact_lock.py (section C); output build/emu_contact_request_proof.txt.
  a-EMULATED - the keyframe arithmetic itself: channel 5 gives frame = round(((raw>>13 & 0x3ff)+2)*2 / scale * fps/60) and channel 3 gives frame = round((word & 0x1fff)*2 / scale * fps/60), verified by round-tripping chosen frames through the real accessors 0x143e99e20 and 0x143e99b70.
  b-DISASSEMBLY - xmm6 is written once at 0x143f00e13 and used for nothing else in the function except the four 'movaps xmm2,xmm6' copies.
  NOT CLAIMED - what the stock lock is in seconds. The raw keyframes live in cpk_dat/common/anime/Mbinfo/bin/CancelData.bin, not in the exe. This pack halves the lock; it is not known what it halves FROM.

WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERYONE, human and CPU alike. Stagger::vf14 contains no controlled-player test.

WHAT YOU SHOULD SEE IN ONE MATCH. Every stagger becomes about twice as quick to play out of, for every action - trapping, shooting, carrying on. It should feel like the stumble stops owning you halfway through.

WHAT WOULD MEAN IT IS TOO FAR. Contact reading as cosmetic - the knock plays but the player is already doing something else underneath it, so the animation and the loss of control stop lining up. At 2.0f that is a real possibility. If you see it, step down to the 1.5f cell rather than reverting outright, because the direction is probably still right.

EXPECTED EFFECT ON FOULS AND CARDS: none directly.

COLLISIONS. Site 0x143f00e13 verified byte-identical between the INSTALLED image and eFootball.exe.PRISTINE this pass (F30F10359DF49403). No overlap with any of the 26 applied specs. DO NOT APPLY WITH contact-dribble-cancel-early.json - they multiply. Emulated: stock Dribble gate 48, this pack alone 24, the headline pack alone 16, BOTH TOGETHER 8. That is a 6x change and you will not be able to attribute what you feel to either one.

REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/contact-cancel-window-x2.json

patches.name: Stagger::vf14 keyframe scale 1.0f -> 2.0f (disp32 re-aim, shared cell NOT written)
patches.note: movss xmm6,[rip+0x394f49d -> 0x1478502b8 = 1.0f] re-aimed to [rip+0x394f675 -> 0x147850490 = 2.0f] inside match::anime::action::Stagger::vf14 (0x143f00de0). xmm6 is the animation playback-speed divisor and is copied into xmm2 before all four keyframe queries in the function, so every cancel gate in a stagger halves. The 1.0f source cell has 13,240 referrers image-wide and is NEVER written - only this instruction's displacement changes. Both cells report writers=0 in tools/exe_census.py.
